videoIdeas.title: Stop saying 'um' — the Prophetic fix
videoIdeas.hook: You don't have a confidence problem. You have a silence problem.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your 'Slow. Clear. Three times.' post (1,982 views) proved there's appetite for Prophetic-method public speaking content, and it's your most under-served pillar — only two posts touch it. doctordaanish is cleaning up with save-able 'how to fix X' practical content, so marry that format to your lane.
videoIdeas.script:
You don't have a confidence problem. You have a silence problem.

Every time you reach for an 'um' or a 'like', what you're actually doing is filling a pause you're too scared to let sit.

The Prophet ﷺ was known to pause. Deliberately. He let the words land before moving on. Silence wasn't weakness, it was weight.

So next time your brain reaches for a filler word, don't replace it with another word. Replace it with nothing. Close your mouth. Count one second. Then speak.

It feels like forever to you. To the room, it sounds like someone who knows exactly what they're saying.

Try it in your next conversation, not your next talk. That's where the habit is actually built.

visuals.setting: Plain wall or a mosque/library corner, mid-shot, you standing or seated. Clean button-up or simple neutral jumper. Calm, unhurried energy — the delivery itself should model the pauses you're teaching.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'um... like... you know...' typed out and then each word getting struck through / deleted one by one as you start speaking.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open: you deliberately pause for a full 2 seconds of silence on camera before the first word, caption 'watch this'
Pattern interrupt — snap your fingers once on the word 'nothing' to mark the pause
On-screen counter ticking '1 second' during a held silence to visualise the technique

videoIdeas.title: 5 things to sort out before you turn 25
videoIdeas.hook: Nobody is coming to build your life for you. Here are five things to stop outsourcing.
videoIdeas.rationale: doctordaanish's 'if you're in your 20s save this' format pulled 93k views and 5.5k likes — pure save-bait listicle. You have zero listicle/save content, which is a clear gap. Done in your blunt older-brother voice it won't read like a recycled coach post.
videoIdeas.script:
Nobody is coming to build your life for you. Here are five things to stop outsourcing before you're 25.

One. Your opinions. If you can't explain why you believe something without quoting a reel, you don't believe it, you're renting it.

Two. Your money. Not investing advice — just know where it goes. Most of you have no idea.

Three. Your circle. You are being formed by five people whether you chose them or not. Choose them.

Four. Your voice. Learn to speak in a room full of people who disagree with you. That skill decides your next ten years.

Five. Your deen. Not inherited habits. A relationship you'd keep even if your parents weren't watching.

Save this. Then actually do one of them this week.

visuals.setting: Walking-and-talking outdoors, or seated at a desk with notebook visible — practical, grounded setting. Everyday smart clothing. Energy is direct and slightly urgent, like you're giving a younger sibling a talking-to.
visuals.visualHook: Big on-screen number counter '1 → 5' with each point snapping onto screen as a short bold caption, so viewers feel the save-value in the first 2 seconds.
otherHookIdeas: On-screen text punchline first: 'By 25 most of you will have outsourced your entire life' then reveal the list
Cold open mid-sentence on point three to create a 'wait, what was one and two' rewind
Hold up a written list on paper and tear off the top as a physical pattern interrupt

videoIdeas.title: You can be struggling and still be grateful
videoIdeas.hook: You can be grateful and still be exhausted. Both are true.
videoIdeas.rationale: lifeofdinoo's two-line reframe format ('You can pray and still need help. Both can be true.') hit 52k views with almost no caption. It's the highest ceiling format in the niche right now and you post nothing like it — everything you post is long-form argument. Test the short punch.
videoIdeas.script:
You can be grateful and still be exhausted. Both are true.

We've turned gratitude into a stick to beat ourselves with. The second you feel tired, someone reminds you people have it worse. As if your struggle needs a permission slip.

Allah gave you emotions. He didn't tell you to perform constant happiness to prove your iman.

You can thank Him for what you have and still ask Him to lift what's heavy. The two live in the same dua.

Stop editing your honesty to sound more spiritual.

visuals.setting: Tight, close, intimate framing — slightly dim, calm. No walking, minimal movement. Let the words carry it. Plain dark top. Quiet, lower-energy delivery than your political posts.
visuals.visualHook: Stark on-screen text 'Both are true.' held on a near-still frame for the first 3 seconds before you speak.
otherHookIdeas: Two contrasting captions appearing on left/right of screen ('grateful' | 'exhausted') then merging
Cold open with you mid-exhale, tired expression, then the line lands
Minimalist black background with only the key sentence typing out in sync with your voice

videoIdeas.title: Technology upgrades itself. You don't.
videoIdeas.hook: Your phone got smarter this year. Did you?
videoIdeas.rationale: Your 'New model every September. Same habits every morning.' post is your third-highest performer (4,733 views, 169 likes) and clearly your strongest original-concept post. Mine the same vein with a sharper angle instead of letting a proven concept sit as a one-off.
videoIdeas.script:
Your phone got smarter this year. Did you?

Every September there's a new model. Faster chip, better camera, and millions of people queue overnight to upgrade a device.

Meanwhile the same person is carrying it. Same temper. Same scroll habit. Same excuses from 2023.

Technology moves forward on its own. You don't get that luxury. People aren't upgraded, they're formed — slowly, deliberately, one habit at a time.

Nobody queues overnight for that. It doesn't come in a box. But it's the only upgrade that actually changes your life.

So — what's the last thing you upgraded in yourself?

visuals.setting: Hold a phone as a prop, then set it down pointedly. Clean modern-ish background, mid-shot. Measured, reflective tone — this is a thinking-out-loud piece, not a rant.
visuals.visualHook: Open on you holding up a phone to camera, on-screen text 'new model' — then flip to point at yourself with text 'same habits'.
otherHookIdeas: Pattern interrupt: slam the phone face-down on the table on the line 'you don't get that luxury'
On-screen text punchline 'you were not upgraded, you were formed' as a mid-video beat
Cold open on the question 'Did you?' before explaining what you mean

videoIdeas.title: The first line of your talk is already won or lost
videoIdeas.hook: Your talk fails in the first ten seconds. Not the middle.
videoIdeas.rationale: Public speaking is your thinnest pillar despite clear engagement, and historical framing is your signature move (Andalusia, Tariq bin Ziyad, Anas ibn Malik posts). Combine a concrete, teachable public speaking lesson with the historical lens you already win with.
videoIdeas.script:
Your talk fails in the first ten seconds. Not the middle.

Most people open with 'Bismillah, um, so today I wanted to talk about…' and they've already lost the room. You just told everyone to relax, nothing important is happening yet.

The khutab that moved entire cities didn't open with warm-up. Tariq bin Ziyad stood in front of an army with the sea behind them and the enemy in front. His first words were the whole argument.

You don't need a sea. You need to delete your warm-up.

Start with the sentence you were building to. Say the thing first. Earn the right to explain it after.

Write your next opening line. Then delete everything before it.

visuals.setting: Standing, slightly more upright and commanding posture — you're demonstrating authority. Neutral backdrop or a lectern-adjacent setup. Firm, confident energy.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'Bismillah, um, so basically...' then a big red line crossing it out with SFX in the first 2 seconds.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open delivering a weak waffly intro, then cut hard and say 'that's why you lost them'
On-screen countdown '10... 9... 8...' to literalise the ten-second window
Split-screen 'weak open' vs 'strong open' demo of the same point

videoIdeas.title: Deen and career were never two separate things
videoIdeas.hook: Ibn Sina would not understand the phrase 'secular job'.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your Ibn Sina / 'secular job' post (1,753 views) landed and taps a real tension for your young Muslim audience. Reframe it toward leadership and vocation — a direction none of your competitors own, and it builds your 'formation' brand rather than chasing political reach.
videoIdeas.script:
Ibn Sina would not understand the phrase 'secular job'.

Neither would al-Biruni. Or Ibn al-Nafis. These men mapped the human body and the stars while deepening their deen. To them it was one life, not two timetables.

We inherited the wall. Deen over here, career over there. Work on Monday, religion on Friday. Most of us didn't choose that split — we were handed it and never questioned it.

But leadership in this Ummah has never come from people who clock out of their faith to go earn. It came from people who saw their work as part of their worship.

You don't need a 'religious job'. You need to stop pretending your current one has nothing to do with Allah.

What would change about your work tomorrow if you believed that?

visuals.setting: Desk or workspace setting — laptop, books, maybe in work clothes to literalise the 'career' half. Thoughtful, grounded tone, not preachy. Mid-shot.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'secular job' with a question-mark glitch effect, while you say the Ibn Sina line.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on the three names appearing one by one as on-screen text before you speak
Visual split of a prayer mat and a laptop merging into one frame
On-screen punchline mid-video: 'you inherited the wall. you didn't build it.'

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 8,579 views and 208 likes — your highest-liked post. The hook 'Can't believe we're still discussing the necessity of protests in 2026' works because it opens mid-frustration and dates itself to right now, which signals urgency. The blunt tone is exactly your voice and the audience rewarded it with the best like-to-view ratio of any top post.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 12 comments despite the like count — the caption makes a statement but never hands the audience a question or a side to pick. Even one sharp closing prompt ('Which camp are you actually in?') would've converted that agreement into the comment volume that pushes reach further.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 4,733 views, 169 likes — your strongest non-political post and proof your mindset/formation lane can perform without a news hook. 'New model every September. Same habits every morning.' is a clean, original parallel and the closing question 'What's the last thing you upgraded in yourself?' is likely why engagement held. This is your most repeatable concept.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 7 comments for 169 likes means the question landed softer than it could. The caption trails off ('Reflections from @') — a cut-off attribution weakens the close. Lead the comment prompt earlier and sharper, and don't let the strongest idea end on a truncated credit line.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your best public speaking post — 'Slow. Clear. Three times. 1,400 years before anyone wrote a book on public speaking, the method was already there' is a brilliant hook that fuses teachable skill with Islamic history, your two strengths. It carves out a lane none of your competitors occupy.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 1,982 views and 3 comments — underperforming its quality, which tells me distribution, not content, is the issue. This pillar needs volume and consistency to train the algorithm; one post can't establish it. Series it up ('Prophetic public speaking, part 2') so the audience learns to expect and search for it.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: The Ibn Sina / 'secular job' angle (1,753 views) hits a genuine tension for young Muslims about faith and career, and 'We built the wall between deen and career much later. Most of us just inherited it' is a sharp, quotable reframe — classic older-brother bluntness.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Zero comments. The caption closes on a diagnosis ('we inherited it') but never turns it back on the viewer, so there's nothing to respond to. End on a personal challenge or question about their own work, and the subject matter is strong enough to spark real debate in the comments.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 24 comments on only 1,749 views — the best comment-to-view ratio in your whole top set. 'Don't let sectarianism blind you to the horrors that occurred in our Ummah' is short, direct, and touches a nerve, which proves controversy-adjacent reminders drive conversation for you.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 42 likes against 24 comments suggests the comments were argumentative rather than affirming — fine for reach, but make sure your on-screen delivery and caption frame your actual position clearly so you're steering the debate, not just lighting it. A one-line statement of where you stand protects the message from being hijacked in the replies.
